variants.title: Capacity must be reserved across asynchronous admission
variants.invariant: Pending work plus dispatched reservations stays within the configured account capacity.
variants.activation: An entrypoint checks a quota before an external height/proof request; its callback creates the record.
variants.sequence: Submit two distinct replacements before either callback; both observe the same free slot.
variants.evidence: Show both accepted records, a sequential rejection control, and marginal excess storage against one allowed replacement.
variants.recovery: Exercise losing PendingSign siblings and the actual cleanup caller; distinguish relayer-only cleanup from permissionless cleanup.
variants.exclusions: A bounded same-owner RBF family does not prove unbounded growth, forced MPC work, or third-party disruption.
variants.fix: Reserve before dispatch, release on failure, and revalidate capacity at insertion without double charging.

variants.title: Refund outputs need chain-specific post-fee validity
variants.invariant: An admitted refund can produce a usable output after fees.
variants.activation: Default or custom fees can leave a positive but sub-policy output.
variants.sequence: Choose amount just above the fee; execution builds a dust output that ordinary relaying rejects.
variants.evidence: Test fee-minus-one, fee, fee-plus-one, and script-specific output bounds using the pinned chain policy.
variants.recovery: Trace rejection and cleanup independently; the orphaned-marker defect is SAT-29, including for non-dust outputs.
variants.exclusions: Relay dust policy is not universally a consensus prohibition; direct miner inclusion and script differences matter.
variants.fix: Validate post-fee output value at admission and execution against the configured chain and script.

variants.title: Mint success can survive a dead bookkeeping callback
variants.invariant: Every issued token liability has registered backing or an authenticated recoverable registration state.
variants.activation: Replay reservation, external mint, and backing registration occur in different receipts.
variants.sequence: Mint commits; the later callback fails for storage balance or gas; the marker survives while inventory is absent.
variants.evidence: Demonstrate durable transferable tokens, the callback failure reason, absent inventory, and blocked retry after funding; measure gas separately from storage.
variants.recovery: Reconcile the exact token issuance and outpoint before idempotent finalization; never clear the marker and mint again blindly.
variants.exclusions: Real deposited BTC remains in custody: missing spendable inventory alone is not fabricated BTC backing or direct theft.
variants.fix: Persist operation context and provide bounded, funded, idempotent finalization after verified mint success.

variants.title: Supply equality does not prove allocation integrity
variants.invariant: Every legitimate holder receives its entitlement exactly once, not once per supplied occurrence.
variants.activation: Migration accepts a caller-provided holder vector and checks only the sum of queried balances.
variants.sequence: Repeat one holder and omit others so the occurrence-weighted sum still equals total supply.
variants.evidence: Use unequal holder balances, all-equal duplicates, and an honest unique-list control; inspect ownership as well as supply.
variants.recovery: A cutover must not strand omitted holders on a token the bridge no longer accepts.
variants.exclusions: Preserve the DAO/MigrationOperator prerequisite; this is not arbitrary public theft.
variants.fix: Reject duplicate identifiers before queries and reconcile a complete, consistent holder snapshot.

variants.title: One-shot migration hits independent runtime limits
variants.invariant: Every supported holder population can complete allocation-preserving migration.
variants.activation: All balances are queried and all mints batched without persisted progress; each call must sum to total supply.
variants.sequence: Grow or fragment the holder set beyond action, dependency, or prepaid-gas bounds; smaller independent calls fail the supply equality.
variants.evidence: Pin runtime limits; derive promise gas, receipt actions, and input dependencies separately; test boundary-minus-one/boundary/plus-one.
variants.recovery: Verify resumable batches bind snapshot, source/destination token, epoch, processed holders, and reconciled totals.
variants.exclusions: Historical 100-action and gas figures are not universal constants. Failed oversized receipts do not execute a successful prefix of their actions.
variants.fix: Use bounded idempotent batches and activate the destination only after complete snapshot reconciliation.

variants.title: Unknown mint outcome is neither success nor safe refund
variants.invariant: Settlement follows proven token delivery; uncertainty cannot authorize duplicate issuance or refund.
variants.activation: A helper recognizes only decoded zero as failure and negates that test to infer success.
variants.sequence: Feed outer failure, malformed/oversized result, zero, partial, full, and over-range amounts through the exact pinned ABI.
variants.evidence: Separate a known pre-mint rejection from a failed outer chain that may include a committed mint; trace token balances and each receipt.
variants.recovery: Keep ambiguous outcomes pending and reconcile issuance before mint retry or source-chain refund.
variants.exclusions: Ordinary receiver panic or malformed receiver output may resolve to valid zero under NEP-141; self-selected bridge recipients do not prove a third-party trigger.
variants.fix: Use explicit known-before-mint failure, delivered, partial, and unresolved states with operation-bound recovery.

variants.title: Dependency rotation has an in-flight authority policy
variants.invariant: A proof result is accepted under the request-generation policy actually promised by the protocol.
variants.activation: A mutable trusted verifier can be rotated while a proof request is in flight.
variants.sequence: Dispatch to A, rotate to B, then deliver A's result; determine whether rotation promises revocation of old requests.
variants.evidence: Identify the verifier, generation, decision receipt, callback window, pause behavior, and compromise assumption.
variants.recovery: Reject or explicitly grandfather old generations; support retry through the authorized verifier without double settlement.
variants.exclusions: A trusted dependency compromise and a short already-dispatched window are conditional assumptions, not evidence the production verifier is compromised.
variants.fix: Bind request identity and generation where revocation is required; otherwise document grandfathering and incident-response limits.

variants.title: A live migration snapshot can duplicate one economic claim
variants.invariant: A snapshotted balance cannot fund both an old-token withdrawal and a replacement-token entitlement.
variants.activation: Migration reads balances asynchronously while old-token ingress remains active and pending operations omit funding-token identity.
variants.sequence: Snapshot a holder, accept its old-token withdrawal, mint the copied replacement balance, cut over, then settle the withdrawal.
variants.evidence: Prove a reachable receipt ordering; distinguish observed calls from simulated balances or printed payouts; inspect both burn-success and burn-failure branches.
variants.recovery: Drain or reconcile old liabilities before cutover; settle each pending withdrawal against its original token and epoch.
variants.exclusions: A migration-only lock does not stop user withdrawals. Conversely, a documented, enforced pause-and-drain process may close this path.
variants.fix: Require quiescence before the snapshot and bind token/epoch to all pending value operations.

variants.title: Per-account limits are not evidence of global overload
variants.invariant: Shared resource admission remains usable under the documented economic and capacity model.
variants.activation: Many accounts can each create funded work, with a finite shared UTXO pool.
variants.sequence: Measure attacker-controlled reservations across accounts and compare locked shared liquidity with committed attacker capital.
variants.evidence: Demonstrate disproportionate cost or an actual victim failure; distinguish expected concurrent users from an attack.
variants.recovery: Exercise signing, replacement, cancellation, and release rather than assuming pending means unrecoverable.
variants.exclusions: The absence of a global cap is not itself a vulnerability; adding one can create a global blocking slot.
variants.fix: Choose bounds, collateral, fairness, or recovery from demonstrated bottlenecks rather than requiring a universal global counter.

variants.title: Parsed Orchard data is not verified authorization
variants.invariant: Consensus-invalid caller data cannot irrecoverably reserve shared withdrawal liquidity.
variants.activation: The bridge recovers recipient/value from an Orchard bundle without verifying all required authorization.
variants.sequence: Verify a valid original bundle, mutate its proof while preserving recipient/value, then submit it to reserve pooled UTXOs.
variants.evidence: Use the exact active circuit/verifier, honest withdrawal control, fully backed token distribution, and measured input-value-to-escrow amplification.
variants.recovery: Exercise signing through PendingVerify and the real replacement/cancellation path; distinguish inability to confirm from inability to recover.
variants.exclusions: A test stopping at PendingSign does not prove signing cannot proceed or that all recovery is impossible.
variants.fix: Validate proof, required authorization signatures and transaction binding before durable reservation, or use an authenticated verifier plus safe recovery.

variants.title: Confirmation and spendability are separate checks
variants.invariant: Assets classified as active backing meet source-chain spendability requirements.
variants.activation: A bridge accepts coinbase outputs using ordinary confirmation tiers.
variants.sequence: Supply an included immature coinbase output; observe issuance and active-inventory classification.
variants.evidence: Detect the coinbase structure, use transaction index zero, and compare maturity boundary controls; pin the chain's counting convention.
variants.recovery: Quarantine immature backing or defer admission until the source-chain maturity rule is met.
variants.exclusions: A mock inclusion response proves bridge handling only. A victim selecting an already-reserved UTXO does not isolate immaturity impact.
variants.fix: Enforce the source chain's coinbase maturity independently of normal value-based confirmation tiers.

variants.title: Optional restrictions and persistent policy are not missing authorization
variants.invariant: Acceptance matches the documented distinction between trust membership and optional restrictions.
variants.activation: A DAO whitelist and message-template map have separate lifecycles.
variants.sequence: Test absent templates, removal, and re-whitelisting; compare resulting acceptance with the intended unrestricted or retained-policy mode.
variants.evidence: Establish whether templates are restrictions or permissions and whose tokens the message can affect.
variants.recovery: Verify separate template removal exists and that non-whitelisted receivers remain blocked.
variants.exclusions: The project confirmed optional templates and retained restrictions are intentional; clearing templates may make reactivation less restricted.
variants.fix: Document and test the intended modes; require mandatory templates only when the target's policy actually demands them.

variants.title: Attached surplus needs a payer and disposition
variants.invariant: Every accepted attached amount is consumed, refunded, or credited under a documented policy.
variants.activation: Admission accepts at least a fixed allowance but failure refunds only that allowance.
variants.sequence: Attach exact and excess amounts on successful and failed operations; inspect payer balances and any credit.
variants.evidence: Read the actual denomination and configured requirement; do not import the report's inconsistent 1.2 versus 0.0012 NEAR figures.
variants.recovery: Check all failure branches and whether the original attached amount and predecessor payer survive callbacks.
variants.exclusions: Self-directed bounded overpayment is not third-party reserve theft; intentionally documented fees are not surplus.
variants.fix: Reject excess or record and refund/credit it to the actual payer, with failure-safe settlement.

variants.title: Retries must not multiply risk accounting
variants.invariant: A unique source outpoint contributes to cumulative confirmation accounting at most as intended.
variants.activation: A pre-mint ring increment survives while mint failure clears only the replay marker.
variants.sequence: Repeat a zero-result safe mint, then submit a distinct same-block victim deposit near a tier boundary.
variants.evidence: Use a concrete mint-failure trigger and a one-attempt control; prove committed increments and separate blocks.
variants.recovery: Compensation must target the same height/amount and not decrement a reused ring slot belonging to another block.
variants.exclusions: A confirmation-check panic rolls back that receipt's tentative increment; not every same-block deposit is delayed.
variants.fix: Use outpoint-idempotent accounting or operation-bound reversal without weakening pre-mint confirmation admission.

variants.title: Partial token use preserves the user's remainder
variants.invariant: Delivered value plus recoverable user credit equals the user's intended entitlement.
variants.activation: Safe mint uses transfer-call with the bridge as sender and treats every positive used amount as full success.
variants.sequence: A receiver accepts part; the resolver returns the remainder to the bridge; no user claim is recorded.
variants.evidence: Resolve used-versus-unused polarity from the pinned ABI and test zero, partial, full, and out-of-range values.
variants.recovery: Attribute the returned remainder to its depositor and token; check retry, refund, lost-and-found, and fee paths.
variants.exclusions: The project acknowledges an all-or-zero integration requirement; establish whether a partial receiver is supported/reachable before scoring.
variants.fix: Reconcile partial use with an explicit user credit/refund, or enforce a safe all-or-zero integration contract.

variants.title: Rejecting issuance must not erase legitimate recovery
variants.invariant: An unminted recoverable source output retains a safe terminal spend or refund path.
variants.activation: Below-minimum deposits are marked processed and parked outside normal inventory.
variants.sequence: Compare refund before verification with standard/safe verification, then lower the minimum and attempt all recovery paths.
variants.evidence: Use an output that can cover fees; distinguish a bridge policy minimum from actual dust or uneconomic refund value.
variants.recovery: Check existing refund execution as well as new requests and prevent concurrent mint/refund during recovery.
variants.exclusions: Intentional no-mint behavior does not prove no-refund intent; extremely small transfers may legitimately be uneconomic.
variants.fix: Reject before consuming the marker or retain an authenticated recoverable unavailable-output state.

variants.title: Overlapping migration executions require independent idempotency
variants.invariant: One source migration allocation is minted no more than once across retries and concurrent operators.
variants.activation: Configuration cutover occurs only after asynchronous mints; no migration lock or completion identity exists.
variants.sequence: Start two authorized migrations before either resolves and compare destination balances and supply.
variants.evidence: Use real destination mint results; respect atomicity of actions within a single receipt instead of assuming partial execution.
variants.recovery: After an ambiguous resolver outcome, reconcile completed destination issuance before retrying.
variants.exclusions: This requires an authorized operator; it is distinct from SAT-08's user race during one migration.
variants.fix: Reserve a unique migration epoch before dispatch and track idempotent completed allocations and cutover.

variants.title: Winning transaction cleanup includes every losing phase
variants.invariant: Finalizing a transaction family releases obsolete descendants and their account signing capacity.
variants.activation: Cleanup handles PendingVerify siblings but omits PendingSign children.
variants.sequence: Create an unsigned replacement/cancel, finalize the original, and attempt a fresh withdrawal.
variants.evidence: Show retained records and indexes, the exact quota failure, and caller permissions of each cleanup method.
variants.recovery: Test original-wins, replacement-wins, repeated cleanup, and a user without relayer privileges.
variants.exclusions: Relayer-recoverable withdrawal unavailability is not automatically permanent token freezing.
variants.fix: Remove obsolete descendants and coupled indexes across phases, or expose authenticated safe orphan cleanup.

variants.title: Resizing security history cannot silently forget its meaning
variants.invariant: A security decision handles evicted history consistently with the accepted confirmation policy.
variants.activation: A bounded ring grows and an evicted height now maps to an empty cell.
variants.sequence: Record a deposit, evict with a colliding verified deposit, grow capacity, then submit a delayed same-height output.
variants.evidence: Pin the PR/revision that contains the ring; compare actual cumulative exposure with the selected tier.
variants.recovery: Preserve a forgotten-history watermark or use an explicit conservative policy across configuration changes.
variants.exclusions: Time alone does not evict this ring. Under-confirmation is not proof of a reorg/double spend; the project accepted the bounded policy tradeoff.
variants.fix: Make resize semantics explicit and test them against the chosen risk policy; document any deliberate relaxation.

variants.title: Universal validation over an empty vector proves nothing
variants.invariant: Replacement transactions satisfy structural constraints before committing cancellation state.
variants.activation: A replacement constructor omits the nonempty-output guard enforced by the original constructor.
variants.sequence: Submit an empty output list; per-output checks pass vacuously.
variants.evidence: Compare original/replacement constructors and trace the actual authorized call and resulting state.
variants.recovery: Check whether the already-signed original remains confirmable and verifiable before claiming a terminal lock.
variants.exclusions: Operator-only malformed input and a surviving original support operational hardening, not an established public fund-loss exploit.
variants.fix: Validate required cardinality at replacement construction and admission, before durable state changes.

variants.title: Compensation must use the asset that funded the operation
variants.invariant: Cleanup burns or refunds the same token generation used by the initiating receipt.
variants.activation: A safe mint reads token A at dispatch, while cleanup rereads mutable configuration after rotation to B.
variants.sequence: Return a full unused amount across cutover and inspect the actual burn target and balances on A and B.
variants.evidence: Establish rotation reachability, token balances, and receipt timing; separate wrong-asset bookkeeping from proven insolvency/profit.
variants.recovery: Drain pending operations before rotation or retain token/epoch identity through cleanup and retries.
variants.exclusions: The project removed migration entrypoints and does not plan rotation; retain this as a conditional future-change check.
variants.fix: Persist immutable funding-token identity for every external effect and its compensation.

variants.title: Repeated embedded payloads amplify storage and callback work
variants.invariant: Persistent representation does not duplicate unused variable-length transaction data across every output without a justified budget.
variants.activation: Each change or migrated UTXO embeds a full signed transaction that consumers do not require.
variants.sequence: Finalize transactions with many outputs and large payloads, then measure storage, view response sizes, and callback work.
variants.evidence: Trace actual readers and repeated clone sites; use realistic maximum payloads and core-operation bounds.
variants.recovery: Plan compatibility for already-stored records and existing off-chain consumers.
variants.exclusions: Unused bytes alone are an efficiency observation unless material cost, undercharge, or liveness is shown.
variants.fix: Store the required outpoint metadata or one shared transaction record; migrate or safely retire legacy payloads.

variants.title: Storage pricing must include legacy variable-length records
variants.invariant: The responsible caller covers actual marginal state cost, including cloned legacy fields.
variants.activation: RBF descendants clone UTXOs while charging one yocto or a fixed estimate based on newer compact records.
variants.sequence: Compare identical input counts using fresh deposit UTXOs and old change UTXOs carrying full transaction bytes.
variants.evidence: Measure byte delta, byte cost, deposit, shortfall, family cap, and attacker capital; distinguish all replacements from excess replacements.
variants.recovery: Track payer and refunds across sibling cleanup; test old records after the write format is fixed.
variants.exclusions: A finite RBF limit bounds amplification; a new-write fix does not retroactively shrink historical records.
variants.fix: Charge bounded actual growth or a worst-case estimate that includes every supported stored version, with explicit legacy handling.

variants.title: Expired cancellation can strand both liquidity and fee reservations
variants.invariant: Every reserved transaction family has a safe terminal settlement or rescue path.
variants.activation: Cancellation prevents further replacements while every member can expire without confirming.
variants.sequence: Create a reserved transaction, cancel it, let all competing Zcash candidates expire, then attempt fresh replacement/cancellation.
variants.evidence: Exercise assert-not-canceled separately from replacement-count bounds; inspect locked UTXOs as well as reserved fees.
variants.recovery: Keep reservations until safe resolution; account for every signed/in-flight candidate and inclusion before expiry.
variants.exclusions: An ordinary unconfirmed original can often be rescued. Bitcoin age alone does not invalidate signatures, and late verification can prove timely inclusion.
variants.fix: Allow safe repeated cancellation with fresh expiry and reconcile the family maximum reservation exactly once on winning settlement.

variants.title: Temporary deposit reservations cannot destroy refund rights
variants.invariant: Recoverable mint failure preserves an existing refund entitlement, paid request cost, and elapsed waiting time.
variants.activation: Permissionless rejection interprets an in-flight deposit marker as final settlement.
variants.sequence: Create a refund, reserve deposit verification, reject during the mint window, then resolve mint to zero.
variants.evidence: Compare no-interference and interference runs; inspect deletion, request cost, original timestamp, and renewed timelock.
variants.recovery: Retrying minting is an alternative outcome, not restoration of a previously purchased refund path.
variants.exclusions: Successful finalization and executed requests follow different rules; the demonstrated harm is cost/delay, not necessarily lost BTC.
variants.fix: Separate pending from settled deposits and retain refund state until settlement justifies its removal.

variants.title: Validate refund destinations before irrevocable commitment
variants.invariant: A committed refund destination is parseable and valid for the configured chain/network.
variants.activation: Address derivation or request storage accepts a raw string and parsing first occurs at execution.
variants.sequence: Commit a malformed destination, wait, execute, and repeat; contrast a caller-selected unbound destination.
variants.evidence: Show the parse point, any equality constraint, and the ability or inability to replace the request.
variants.recovery: Check normal deposit finalization separately; authenticate any destination supersession.
variants.exclusions: A pre-mutation panic preserves state and may leave deposit finalization available; do not call all recovery permanently lost.
variants.fix: Parse/network-check at commitment and request time and define authorized repair for legacy invalid destinations.

variants.title: Optimistic beneficiary selection is an explicit trust boundary
variants.invariant: A refund beneficiary follows either verifiable owner authorization or an explicitly accepted optimistic review policy.
variants.activation: A deposit omits a committed refund address and the first requester selects the destination.
variants.sequence: Reconstruct an enumerable/default message or observe published calldata, capture the slot, and model the full review window.
variants.evidence: Identify exact message knowledge, permissions, veto, finalization guard, retry cost, active timelock, and attacker-controlled beneficiary.
variants.recovery: Distinguish an unexecuted request that can be rejected from post-execution signing; rejection restarts a race rather than proving irreversible denial.
variants.exclusions: The team acknowledged this design and reported a 100-year timelock mitigation; do not claim a timelock bypass or independently verified deployed state.
variants.fix: Bind recipient authorization or committed destination; otherwise document and test the optimistic review assumption and actual disabling configuration.

variants.title: Deleting a request does not revoke signing authority
variants.invariant: Cancellation policy agrees with every pending signing request and externally usable authorization.
variants.activation: Request deletion leaves a pending refund transaction signable by a separate entrypoint.
variants.sequence: Execute, reject, then sign the stale candidate; also test an already-dispatched signing callback.
variants.evidence: Show actual signing authorization, immutable destination, replay protection, and whether a completed signature can still spend.
variants.recovery: Never restore mint eligibility merely because local pending records were removed; external signatures may survive.
variants.exclusions: Signing a refund to the depositor does not alone prove theft or double spend. The project chose to prohibit rejection after execution.
variants.fix: Enforce a non-cancelable in-flight boundary, or implement generation-bound revocation before signature issuance and safe external disposition afterward.

variants.title: Cleanup must not orphan an unsigned refund's replay marker
variants.invariant: A consumed marker always has a completed external disposition or a usable authorized recovery operation.
variants.activation: Executed refunds can be rejected and all unsigned candidates removed while the marker remains.
variants.sequence: Use a valid non-dust refund, execute/reject/clean it, and try mint, new request, re-execution, and signing.
variants.evidence: Prove every usable candidate was removed and no usable signed refund remains; compare rejection before execution.
variants.recovery: Clearing a marker requires reconciling prior and in-flight signatures, not just observing no finalization.
variants.exclusions: Distinct from SAT-02's dust check and SAT-28's surviving signing path; shared cleanup code does not imply identical causality.
variants.fix: Prevent unsafe post-execution rejection or preserve recoverable refund state until the source UTXO disposition is established.

variants.title: Sponsored registration refund ownership
variants.invariant: Released storage value follows the intended sponsor/subsidy policy.
variants.activation: Minting auto-registers recipients using token-contract funds.
variants.sequence: Register, mint, empty, unregister, then repeat a genuinely new sponsored registration.
variants.evidence: Identify sponsor, refund beneficiary, fees that fund the subsidy, and marginal cost.
variants.recovery: Verify safe mint's user-registration path separately.
variants.exclusions: The team accepts standard-flow sponsorship as a fee-funded subsidy; finalized proof replay is not another sponsored registration.
variants.fix: Track sponsorship if refunds must return to the sponsor, or explicitly account for and bound the subsidy.

variants.title: Unassigned output-relaxation remainder
variants.invariant: User entitlement equals external payout, explicit fees, and recoverable remainder.
variants.activation: Output validation tolerates a shortfall while burning only actual payout plus gas.
variants.sequence: Choose the minimum tolerated payout and reconcile BTC custody, supply, bridge tokens, and fee/user ledgers.
variants.evidence: Calculate the unassigned remainder without confusing retained assets with insolvency.
variants.recovery: Find a user credit/refund or a documented intentional fee classification.
variants.exclusions: The report establishes unassigned value, not extraction or insolvency.
variants.fix: Require exact output accounting or explicitly attribute and recover the delta.

variants.title: Host release tooling remains a separate trust surface
variants.invariant: Published artifacts derive from reviewed tools and intended publishing authority.
variants.activation: Workflow actions or host installers use mutable references with release permissions.
variants.sequence: Trace action tags, installer source, permissions, build inputs, and deployment hash comparison.
variants.evidence: Separate reproducible container inputs from mutable host-side execution.
variants.recovery: Verify artifact comparison and recovery of compromised release authority.
variants.exclusions: CI was outside the stated production-contract scope; retain as conditional supply-chain hardening, not a demonstrated compromise.
variants.fix: Pin and verify tools, restrict publishing authority, and verify built/deployed hashes.

variants.title: Configuration combinations need documented semantics
variants.invariant: Accepted configuration combinations support the promised operations.
variants.activation: Zero limits/delays or minimum amounts below fee floors pass validation.
variants.sequence: Exercise zero, minimum, and cross-field combinations through the real update path.
variants.evidence: Identify intentional disable switches and the exact operation affected.
variants.recovery: Verify updates revalidate and recovery remains possible.
variants.exclusions: DAO-controlled choices and intentional zero values are not untrusted-attacker bypasses.
variants.fix: Document allowed modes and validate cross-field requirements without rejecting deliberate disable values.

variants.title: Bounded response reads need compatibility and diagnostics
variants.invariant: Supported responses fit bounds and operational failures remain diagnosable.
variants.activation: MPC callbacks return false without an event on failed/oversized responses.
variants.sequence: Exercise actual supported response encodings immediately below, at, and above the cap.
variants.evidence: Measure the pinned ABI payload and distinguish return-value observability from emitted events.
variants.recovery: Confirm retries remain possible and signature slots are not falsely populated.
variants.exclusions: Response bounds are defensive; missing events alone do not demonstrate attacker-triggered loss.
variants.fix: Document size assumptions, test compatibility, and emit useful failure diagnostics where appropriate.

variants.title: Expiry is about inclusion, not later verification
variants.invariant: Expiry monitoring distinguishes unmined expired transactions from timely inclusion awaiting proof.
variants.activation: Pending views expose serialized transactions without explicit expiry status.
variants.sequence: Compare unmined expiry, inclusion before expiry with late verification, and zero-expiry refunds.
variants.evidence: Pin chain rules and actual configured window; do not generalize illustrative hours or block gaps.
variants.recovery: Exercise replacement/cancel availability at the actual stage.
variants.exclusions: Contracts do not emit an event merely because time advances, and expired unmined status does not imply every recovery is closed.
variants.fix: Expose decoded expiry and monitor inclusion-aware status without rejecting timely included transactions.

variants.title: Refunds follow predecessor payer rather than persistent signer
variants.invariant: Failure compensation returns value to the account that actually funded it.
variants.activation: A forwarding relayer attaches its funds while retaining a different transaction signer.
variants.sequence: Forward a zero-result safe mint and inspect the storage refund recipient.
variants.evidence: Prove a deployed authorized forwarding contract and unintended sponsorship, not merely a hypothetical identity difference.
variants.recovery: Carry the storage payer through every callback and excess-refund branch.
variants.exclusions: The team reports only direct relayers, where signer equals payer; retain as a conditional test.
variants.fix: Snapshot and authorize the predecessor payer or explicit sponsor at the payable boundary.

variants.title: Sensitive setters need the intended key boundary
variants.invariant: Controller authority and any required deposit-capable-key confirmation are both enforced.
variants.activation: A legacy payout setter is controller-gated but accepts zero deposit.
variants.sequence: Model a restricted function-call key permitted to call the setter and inspect later payout routing.
variants.evidence: Establish active legacy usage and actual receiver/method key permissions.
variants.recovery: Check safe restoration of the payout destination.
variants.exclusions: Missing one yocto alone is hardening unless the key exposure and required confirmation boundary are established.
variants.fix: Use payable plus exact one-yocto validation when required, retaining controller authorization.

variants.title: Deployment initialization needs atomic authority binding
variants.invariant: The first initialization assigns only intended authority.
variants.activation: Public initializers are deployed in a transaction separate from initialization.
variants.sequence: Race a first caller against deployment; compare an atomic deploy-and-init batch.
variants.evidence: Inspect actual deployment transactions and preexisting funds/state assumptions.
variants.recovery: Determine whether redeployment is a complete recovery before asserting loss.
variants.exclusions: Already initialized deployments and atomic batches are negative controls; one-time guards do not authenticate the first caller.
variants.fix: Initialize atomically or authenticate a precommitted deployer/factory.

variants.title: Documentation must reflect receipt-level recovery
variants.invariant: Operational instructions describe actual entrypoints, roles, token placement, and failure recovery.
variants.activation: Docs retain stale method names, permission claims, or whole-transaction rollback language.
variants.sequence: Compare docs with exported methods and standard/safe mint callback behavior.
variants.evidence: Distinguish real lost-and-found credit from clearing a marker for retry.
variants.recovery: Document the actual user/relayer recovery step for each outcome.
variants.exclusions: Documentation drift alone is not an independent runtime exploit.
variants.fix: Correct names, permissions, transfer-call requirements, and non-atomic receipt semantics.
